fieldNotes.title: Field Notes: 47% lift at day 2, -3% at day 14
fieldNotes.source: Anonymous performance marketer at a Bangalore D2C apparel brand
fieldNotes.story:
Variant B was crushing it. Day 2: lift +47% over control. n=200 per arm. Manager said 'declare winner, scale to 100% traffic.' I caved.

Day 14 (post-rollout): aggregated lift over 30,000 users was -3%. We had taken 2 days of noise and called it signal. Worse: variant B was creative-fatigue-prone; lift decayed faster than control. **₹14 lakh of paid spend at -3% efficiency before we caught it.**

The minimum sample size for our ROAS variance was n≈4,700 per arm. Day 2 with n=200 had confidence interval of [-7%, +35%] — the +47% point estimate was within noise. I now run a power calculation BEFORE every test, write the minimum n on the test plan, and refuse to call winners before we hit it.
fieldNotes.takeaway: Day-2 lift is almost always noise; minimum-sample-size discipline before declaring winners is non-negotiable.

bossBattle.title: Boss Battle: declare winner today?
bossBattle.setup: Sneha's running a creative A/B test on Meta. Day 2: variant B leading by 38% lift. Manager wants to scale to 100% traffic for Q2 push. Sneha has 30 minutes to decide.

coach.name: Founder-turned-mentor Manish
coach.role: Built and sold 2 D2C brands; runs ad spend > ₹40cr/yr

stages.prompt: Manager pings: 'B is winning huge. Scale now?' Sneha's first move?

options.label: Calculate the minimum sample size for the variance she's seeing. Probably much larger than current n.
options.explain: Right. Day-2 'huge lift' usually has a CI wide enough to include zero. Power calc first, decision second.

options.label: Yes — scale immediately to capture the lift.
options.explain: Same Bangalore D2C story. ₹14 lakh of regret incoming.

options.label: Reject the test entirely.
options.explain: Overcorrection. The test is fine; the rush is the problem.

stages.prompt: Power calc says minimum n = 4700/arm. Currently at n = 200/arm. What's Sneha's call?

options.label: Continue test until n hits 4700/arm. Set a calendar reminder for the date that lands.
options.explain: Right discipline. Pre-committed ending; no decision until then.

options.label: Compromise: scale variant B to 50% traffic now.
options.explain: Half-measure that still leaks ROAS if B isn't actually winning. Wait for the data.

options.label: Kill the test; pick by gut.
options.explain: Wastes the data already collected. Run it out.

stages.prompt: Day 14: n hit. Lift is +6%, CI [+2%, +10%]. Manager wants 'a bigger win'.

options.label: Ship variant B. +6% with tight CI is a real, sizable win at scale.
options.explain: Right. 6% lift on every ad spend dollar across the year is enormous; manager just expected larger headline.

options.label: Run another 14 days hoping for bigger lift.
options.explain: Diminishing returns; 6% is already a confirmed win. Ship.

options.label: Skip B; design a third variant.
options.explain: Loss aversion. B is the win; keep iterating but ship the win first.

outcomes.perfect: Sneha ships +6% with confidence and CI documented. Manager learns the discipline. ₹14L not lost on day-2 noise.
outcomes.good: Solid run. Discipline holds; +6% shipped. Worth re-running with a creative variant 3 next quarter.
outcomes.learn: Re-read the power-calc section. Day-2 'lift' is usually noise; the math is what tells you.
